messages.content: Simulate shear+density maps (nside 64, f_sky 0.3), measure 3x2pt bandpowers with NaMaster in linear bins of width 20, show measured spectra against input theory.

I simulated the maps and measured all three 3x2pt spectra with NaMaster. Averaged over the bins, the measured bandpowers match the input theory to within about 2% for shear and about 10% for the other two spectra (Figure 15). That is roughly what one random sky at nside 64 should give.

**Simulation (Figure 9)**
- nside 64, polar-cap mask with f_sky = 0.2995, random seed 0.
- Input cosmology: Ω_m = 0.30, σ8 = 0.81, h = 0.67.
- Two tracers, each with a Gaussian n(z):

| Tracer | Kind | n(z) | Bias | Number density | Noise |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| src0 | shear | z_mean 0.9, σ_z 0.25 | n/a | 8 arcmin⁻² | σ_e = 0.26 |
| lens0 | density | z_mean 0.5, σ_z 0.1 | 1.6 | 4 arcmin⁻² | shot noise |

- I chose these tracer settings because you didn't specify any. Shape and shot noise were added to the maps.
- The mask is binary (not apodized), and its effective f_sky is 0.2995 for both fields.

**Bandpowers**
- Linear bins of width 20 starting at ℓ = 2. The tool stopped at ℓ_max = 128 (twice nside) because bins above that are biased by pixel effects.
- That leaves 6 bandpowers with edges at 2, 22, 42, 62, 82, 102, 129 (the last bin is a little wider), centred at ℓ ≈ 11.5, 31.5, 51.5, 71.5, 91.5 and 115.
- Noise was subtracted analytically from the two auto-spectra.
- Theory was binned with the same bandpower windows as the measurement, so the two are directly comparable.

**Measured vs. input theory (mean over the 6 bins)**

| Spectrum | Measured | Binned theory | Measured / theory |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shear EE (src0 × src0) | 1.45e-8 | 1.42e-8 | ~1.02 |
| Density × shear (lens0 × src0) | 2.76e-7 | 3.03e-7 | ~0.91 |
| Density auto (lens0 × lens0) | 1.56e-5 | 1.69e-5 | ~0.93 |

- I worked out the theory means myself from the six binned values the tool reported. The bin-by-bin comparison, with the B-mode components, is in Figure 15.
- The 7–9% low values for the two density spectra are consistent with cosmic variance. The lowest bins dominate the mean, and with f_sky 0.3 a bin at ℓ ~ 10 averages only about 70 modes, so it scatters by roughly ±15%.
- The simulated B-mode signal is zero, so EB, BE, BB and TB should be consistent with noise. A binary mask leaks some E into B, which is why an apodized mask would be the cleaner choice for B-mode null tests.

The outputs are a sacc file, `namaster_32676c.sacc`, which has the bandpower windows but no covariance yet, plus one CSV per spectrum (`namaster_*_*.csv`). The next step would be to add a covariance, either by passing f_sky,eff = 0.2995 to TJPCov or `sacc_attach_gaussian_covariance`, or with TJPCov's NaMaster-based covariance on the same mask. That would give a χ² test of the agreement instead of comparing by eye.

Files are in `/Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-desc/runs/261022_170849/`:
- `namaster_32676c.sacc`
- `namaster_src0_src0.csv`
- `namaster_lens0_src0.csv`
- `namaster_lens0_lens0.csv`
- `namaster_cls_32676c.png` (Figure 15)
- `sim_maps.png` (Figure 9)

messages.content: For the sacc you measured with NaMaster: generate a TJPCov FourierGaussianFsky covariance config (f_sky from the mask, n_gal, galaxy bias), compute the covariance, compare with plain Knox, report chi2 at input cosmology and whether positive definite.

I'll start by removing the B-mode data types, since TJPCov and firecrown only use the E-mode and density spectra.

I built the TJPCov FourierGaussianFsky covariance and it is positive definite. It agrees with the plain Knox covariance to about 1%, and the measured bandpowers give χ² = 27.7 for 18 points at the input cosmology.

**Inputs**
- I first made a copy of `namaster_32676c.sacc` without the B-mode spectra, keeping 18 points: shear EE, density × shear, and density auto, 6 bandpowers each.
- Both covariances use the same settings, taken from the simulation:
  - f_sky = 0.2995, the effective f_sky of the mask reported in the last turn.
  - Number densities: 8 arcmin⁻² for src0 and 4 arcmin⁻² for lens0.
  - Shape noise σ_e = 0.26 and lens bias 1.6.
  - Cosmology Ω_m = 0.30, σ8 = 0.81, h = 0.67.
- TJPCov binned the covariance with the bandpower windows stored in the sacc file. It ran locally in 1.9 s and has the Gaussian term only.

**TJPCov vs. Knox (Figure 25)**

| | Knox | TJPCov |
|---|---|---|
| Positive definite | yes | yes |
| Minimum eigenvalue | 1.11e-20 | 1.11e-20 |
| Condition number | 1.03e9 | 1.01e9 |
| Total S/N | 64.3 | 64.9 |
| Median σ ratio, TJPCov/Knox (shear EE / density × shear / density auto) | – | 0.991 / 0.989 / 0.991 |
| Smallest σ ratio (same order) | – | 0.88 / 0.94 / 0.97 |
| Largest difference between the two correlation matrices | – | 0.026 |

- The two covariances are the same to about 1%. The few-percent to 12% differences are probably in the lowest-ℓ bins, where TJPCov integrates over the bandpower windows and Knox uses one effective Δℓ per bin. Knox's per-bin Δℓ ranged from 18.7 to 26.8.
- The condition number of about 10⁹ only reflects that the density and shear spectra differ in amplitude by about 10³. It is not a numerical problem.
- The correlation matrix is in Figure 23. The largest correlation between different points is 0.78, which comes from pairs of spectra in the same ℓ bin.

**χ² at the input cosmology** (lens0 bias 1.6, no other systematics)

| Spectrum | χ² with TJPCov | χ² with Knox |
|---|---|---|
| Shear EE (src0 × src0) | 8.1 / 6 | 7.9 / 6 |
| Density × shear (src0 × lens0) | 5.4 / 6 | 5.1 / 6 |
| Density auto (lens0 × lens0) | 8.6 / 6 | 8.4 / 6 |
| **Total** | **27.7 / 18 (1.54 per point)** | **26.1 / 18 (1.45 per point)** |

- The largest single deviation is 2.1σ, and the RMS deviation is 1.1σ. Data vs. theory with these error bars is in Figure 31.
- I estimate the probability of a χ² at least this large for 18 points at about 7% (TJPCov) and 10% (Knox), so the input theory is acceptable. I worked these probabilities out myself; the tools did not report them.
- A slightly high χ² is expected here. The mask is binary and not apodized, so neighbouring bandpowers are coupled, and neither f_sky covariance includes that coupling. Both therefore somewhat underestimate the errors in the lowest bins. TJPCov's NaMaster-based covariance on `sim_mask.fits` would include the coupling and should lower the χ².
